source.title: Causality and Advanced Models in Trip Mode Prediction: Interest in Choosing Swissmetro
source.authors: Huy Pham; Xuan Jiang; Cong Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses the double-descent hypothesis and compares model accuracy, but does not test a double-descent curve or any of the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports prediction accuracy for a neural network and a multinomial logit model, and qualitatively notes sensitivity to increased noise. It does not report test-error sweeps over model size, epochs, or sample size, locate an interpolation threshold, or measure a peak. Its statement about fitting data with low training loss is not a test-error result. Causal-inference results do not bear on the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper frames itself as exploring the double-descent hypothesis, but reports only single accuracy numbers for one neural network (about 67%) and one multinomial logit model (44%). There is no sweep over model size, epochs or samples, no interpolation threshold, and no test-error curve. A two-model accuracy comparison cannot show a second descent, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors report about 67% accuracy for the network versus 44% for the multinomial logit, and take this as overparameterization helping prediction "to some extent". Their formal conclusions concern only the causal inference: adjusting for confounders strengthened survey location as a predictor, and using gender as an instrumental variable strengthened high income as a predictor. The conclusions do not claim to establish a double-descent curve.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a two-layer neural network with random features against a multinomial logit utility model. It does not reproduce the original double-descent size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors qualitatively report greater neural-network sensitivity as noise increases; no quantitative settings or outcome differences are given.

fits_no_version.finding: The two-layer network had about 67% accuracy versus 44% for the regularized multinomial logit on Swissmetro (10-fold stratified shuffle split).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On Swissmetro mode choice, an overparameterized two-layer network outperformed a multinomial logit in accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors say the network became more sensitive to real data as the noise level increased; no numbers are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The overparameterized network's sensitivity rises with noise level.

record.problems: The study does not report error curves across model sizes, epochs, or sample sizes, does not identify an interpolation threshold, and gives no quantitative noise-sensitivity results. Accuracy is reported without uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the row limit. The statement that varying random features and kernel size lets the network fit with low training loss is not a test-error result.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep and no test-error peak near the interpolation threshold.
No test error over training epochs.
No capacity sweep past the interpolation point for any model class.
No quantified noise effect on a peak, no multiple peaks, no regularization tuning.

record.verdict_notes: The record's classification as T6/discusses is correct. The paper names double descent as its motivation but runs no experiment able to show it. The 44% logit accuracy is also oddly low for a model with a pseudo R-squared of 0.277, so the accuracy comparison itself is weakly supported.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error curve around an interpolation threshold.
No test-error measurements over training epochs.
No sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep or evidence of risk falling again beyond an interpolation point.
No effective-complexity measure or comparison of peak locations across axes.
Noise sensitivity is mentioned, but the paper does not test whether noise drives a peak, whether peaks split, or whether tuned regularization removes them.
No effective-parameter count or re-expression of a descent curve.
